title: Learning from label proportions for a visual matrix speller (ERP)
description: EEG recordings from 13 healthy participants performing an online copy-spelling task with a visual 6x7 matrix ERP speller. The speller was designed for learning from label proportions (LLP), an unsupervised, calibration-free classification approach for ERP-based brain-computer interfaces. Two stimulus sequences with different target/non-target ratios allowed target and non-target responses to be estimated without labeled data. On average, 84.5% of characters were spelled correctly without prior calibration.
methods_description: Participants spelled a German pangram sentence three times using a visual ERP speller with a 6x7 grid and a 250 ms stimulus onset asynchrony. Each character comprised 68 highlighting events from two sequence types (3 targets in 8 stimuli, and 2 targets in 18 stimuli). EEG was recorded with a BrainAmp DC amplifier and 31 passive Ag/AgCl electrodes in an EasyCap, sampled at 1000 Hz with a nose reference. The LLP classifier was reset at the start of each sentence and retrained after each character.
